title: Active-river forcing admitted at the current management boundary

contrast_postallocation.meaning: Passive groundwater drainage arriving after t=0 allocation did not retroactively alter that day's management decision.

purpose: Test the complementary time-direction case to DUMMY-20E3: an active River exchange is computed by MF6 and published to Ribasim before the t=0 fixed-grid allocation solve, so the negative infiltration forcing should reduce the current t=0 root allocation rather than waiting for the next daily boundary.

active_river.derivation: LevelDemand priority 1 holds Basin at 1.0 m. The t=0 allocation sees the already-published active-river infiltration as implicit negative forcing, leaving 32 - 7.999914667576883 m3/day for root-first UserDemand.

hypotheses: The no-exchange control reproduces the t=0 32/0 m3/day root/external allocation.
In the active-River case, the first MF6 River exchange is published to Ribasim before the t=0 allocation solve.
The t=0 active-River root allocation is approximately 24.0000853324 m3/day and external allocation remains zero.
The allocation reduction relative to control equals the first-interval active-River infiltration rate within tolerance.
External physical delivery remains zero for the one-day root-first case.
Active-River root cumulative physical delivery is materially lower than the no-exchange control because the applied root target is smaller.
At every active-River boundary the MF6 River flux is reciprocal to Ribasim infiltration and the source = root + external + infiltration + Basin-storage ledger closes.

This is the causal complement of DUMMY-20E3: a forcing present before SOLVE affects the current allocation; a forcing arriving after SOLVE affects physical state but not the already admitted allocation.

observability.allocation_authority: Read Ribasim results/allocation.arrow after product finalization. Do not infer allocation solely from physical supply.
observability.physical_authority: XMI cumulative UserDemand inflow, Basin level, Basin cumulative infiltration and MF6 River flux.
